editorial:
The Boogie Man Will Get You is a feature-length horror comedy of about 66 minutes, released by Columbia Pictures on October 22, 1942, directed by Lew Landers. Boris Karloff plays Professor Nathaniel Billings, a scientist running experiments in a New England mansion, and Peter Lorre plays Dr. Arthur Lorencz. Maxie Rosenbloom, Larry Parks and Jeff Donnell round out the cast. According to Wikipedia, it was the final film Karloff made under his contract with Columbia. A creator would want it for the Karloff and Lorre pairing and for its light, quick tone.

The rights trap is that its status as a free-to-use print is not established here. A film published in 1942 is free of copyright only if it had no notice or its renewal was missed in the 1969-1970 window. We could not confirm either point. We did not read the renewal catalogs through to the 'B' entries, and we did not run the Copyright Office records search. Treat the print as unconfirmed until someone checks both. Internet Archive uploads exist, but a copy being posted there proves nothing about its copyright status.
faq: Is The Boogie Man Will Get You in the public domain?

Not confirmed. The film is from 1942, so it is free only if it was never renewed in the 1969-1970 window or lacked a valid notice. We could not complete that check. Search the 1969, 1970 and 1971 Catalog of Copyright Entries volumes and the Copyright Office public records before relying on it.
Can I use the Internet Archive copy in my own project?

Only after the renewal check is done. Both uploads exist and resolve, but we did not confirm their source or their quality. Whether the music or the story carries separate rights was also not checked.
